title: Accenture Computer Networks, TCP/IP, Routing, HTTP, Security & Mobile Computing PYQs
category: Computer Networks / Network Security / Web / Cryptography / Mobile Computing
description: 120 MCQs from the uploaded PYQ PDF. Every option has an individual explanation. Correct answers preserve the green-highlighted answers shown in the source pages.
sourceNote: The answer key is based on the green-highlighted choices in the PDF page images, while the explanations preserve the terminology and framing of the source.

questions.question: What is the fundamental purpose of a computer network?

explanations.A: Networks allow computers and devices to share files, printers, applications, storage, and other resources.
explanations.B: Data storage can be a network service, but it is only one use of a network, not its fundamental purpose.
explanations.C: Networks can distribute computation, but computation itself is not the fundamental purpose of networking.
explanations.D: Security is an important network function, but networking fundamentally enables communication and resource sharing.

questions.question: Which topology does the Internet resemble?

explanations.A: A ring topology connects nodes in a closed loop; it does not describe the Internet's highly interconnected structure.
explanations.B: A bus topology uses one shared backbone cable and is not representative of the Internet.
explanations.C: A star topology has a central device connecting endpoints and is common in LANs, not the Internet as a whole.
explanations.D: A mesh provides many interconnections and is the closest simplified description of the Internet's redundant, interconnected structure.

questions.question: What type of network covers a large geographical area, like a city, country, or the world?

explanations.A: A LAN covers a limited local area such as a home, office, or building.
explanations.B: A MAN generally covers a metropolitan or city-scale area.
explanations.C: A WAN spans large geographic areas and can connect networks across countries or the world.
explanations.D: A PAN is a small personal network around a user and nearby devices.

questions.question: Which device is used to connect different network segments in a computer network?

explanations.A: A repeater regenerates signals to extend a network segment; it does not make routing decisions.
explanations.B: A router forwards packets between different IP networks and can connect separate network segments/networks.
explanations.C: A bridge connects LAN segments at the Data Link layer using MAC addresses.
explanations.D: A modem converts between digital data and the signaling used by a communication medium; it is not primarily a segment-connecting device.

questions.question: What protocol is commonly used for transmitting web pages over the internet?

explanations.A: SMTP is primarily used for sending email, not for transferring web pages.
explanations.B: FTP is designed for file transfer rather than normal web-page retrieval.
explanations.C: HTTP is the application-layer protocol used to request and transfer web resources.
explanations.D: SNMP is used for network monitoring and management.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model ensures the error-free transmission of data?

explanations.A: The Physical layer transmits raw bits; it does not normally provide end-to-end error recovery.
explanations.B: The Data Link layer can detect errors in frames and, depending on the protocol, support link-level recovery.
explanations.C: The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing rather than reliable end-to-end delivery.
explanations.D: The Transport layer can provide reliable end-to-end delivery, especially through TCP.

questions.question: In a computer network, what is the main function of the application layer?

options.A: To provide network services to the applications
options.B: To transmit data between network devices

explanations.A: The Application layer exposes network services such as web, email, naming, and file-transfer services to applications.
explanations.B: Lower layers handle the actual transmission and forwarding of data between network devices.
explanations.C: Encapsulation and segmentation are distributed across several layers rather than being the sole Application-layer function.
explanations.D: Routing is primarily a Network-layer function.

questions.question: Which command can be used to view the current IP configuration of a device?

explanations.A: ipconfig is a Windows command used to display and manage IP configuration.
explanations.B: ifconfig is a traditional Unix/Linux command for viewing and configuring network interfaces.
explanations.C: Both commands can display interface/IP configuration, although they are associated with different operating-system families.
explanations.D: netstat displays network connections, listening ports, routing information, and statistics depending on options.

questions.question: What is the result of executing the ping localhost command?

options.A: It sends ICMP echo requests to the local machine
options.B: It configures the local machine's IP address

explanations.A: ping localhost resolves the loopback destination and sends ICMP Echo Requests to the local host interface.
explanations.B: ping does not configure IP addressing.
explanations.C: Commands such as route, ip route, or netstat -r are used to inspect routing tables.
explanations.D: DNS cache clearing uses operating-system-specific commands; ping does not clear it.

questions.question: If a computer is unable to access the Internet, but can communicate with local network devices, what should be checked first?

explanations.A: If local connectivity works but Internet access fails, the router/default-gateway path is an important item to check.
explanations.B: A cable fault can prevent local connectivity too, so it is less consistent with the stated symptom.
explanations.C: A local firewall can block particular traffic, but the source identifies DNS settings for the described Internet-access symptom.
explanations.D: Incorrect DNS can prevent hostnames from resolving, but the source marks the basic network connection as the first check.

questions.question: A computer can ping IP addresses but not domain names. What is likely the issue?

explanations.A: An IP conflict can disrupt local network communication and is not the most direct explanation when IP-address pings work.
explanations.B: A complete router failure would generally affect broader connectivity, but DNS can fail while IP connectivity remains.
explanations.C: If IP addresses work but domain names fail, name resolution is a prime suspect, usually due to DNS configuration.
explanations.D: A faulty cable would commonly affect both IP and name-based connectivity.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for establishing, managing, and terminating sessions between applications?

explanations.A: The Session layer establishes, manages, and terminates communication sessions between applications.
explanations.B: The Transport layer can provide reliable end-to-end delivery, especially through TCP.
explanations.C: The Application layer provides application-facing network services; session control is separately modeled by the Session layer in OSI.
explanations.D: The Presentation layer handles data representation, translation, compression, and encryption-related transformations.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Network Layer in the OSI model?

options.A: To provide data routing paths for network communication

explanations.A: The Network layer determines paths and forwards packets between networks.
explanations.B: Formatting/representation transformations are associated with the Presentation layer.
explanations.C: Connection establishment is mainly associated with Transport or Session functions depending on the type of connection.
explanations.D: Data encoding/representation transformations are associated with the Presentation layer.

questions.question: In the TCP/IP model, which layer corresponds to the OSI model's Physical and Data Link layers?

explanations.A: The TCP/IP Application layer combines functions represented by several upper OSI layers.
explanations.B: TCP can provide reliability through sequencing, acknowledgments, retransmission, and ordering.
explanations.C: The TCP/IP Internet layer corresponds broadly to OSI Network-layer functions such as IP routing.
explanations.D: The TCP/IP Network Interface/Link layer corresponds broadly to OSI Physical and Data Link functions.

questions.question: The process of encapsulation involves data moving from which layer to which layer?

explanations.A: During encapsulation, data moves down the protocol stack from the Application layer toward the Physical layer.
explanations.B: Moving upward from Physical to Application is decapsulation, not encapsulation.
explanations.C: This is one transition within encapsulation, but not the complete direction asked by the question.
explanations.D: This is an upward/decapsulation direction, not the normal encapsulation direction.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for error detection and correction at the destination?

explanations.A: TCP can provide reliability through sequencing, acknowledgments, retransmission, and ordering.
explanations.B: The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing, but a complete inability to connect should first be checked at the Physical layer.
explanations.C: DHCP uses application-layer messages carried over UDP/IP, but successful Ethernet communication first depends on the Data Link layer being operational.
explanations.D: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.

questions.question: What does the TCP/IP model's Internet layer do?

explanations.A: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.B: This is the answer highlighted in the supplied PYQ and directly addresses the question.
explanations.C: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.D: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.

questions.question: Which protocol operates at the Transport Layer of the OSI model to ensure reliable communication?

explanations.A: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.B: IP provides best-effort packet delivery and routing; it does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.
explanations.C: TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered byte-stream delivery.
explanations.D: UDP is connectionless and does not provide TCP-style reliability or ordering.

questions.question: How does the Presentation Layer of the OSI model differ from the Application Layer?

options.A: It is responsible for session management
options.B: It deals with syntax and semantics of the information exchanged
options.D: It is not implemented in the TCP/IP model

explanations.A: Session management belongs to the Session layer, not the Presentation layer.
explanations.B: The Presentation layer deals with data representation/syntax and translation between formats.
explanations.C: Encryption and compression are commonly associated with Presentation-layer responsibilities in the OSI model.
explanations.D: TCP/IP does not have a separate Presentation layer, but its functions can be implemented within Application-layer protocols.

questions.question: What feature distinguishes TCP from UDP at the Transport Layer?

options.B: TCP and UDP use different port numbers
options.C: TCP is connection-oriented while UDP is not
options.D: TCP uses IP but UDP does not

explanations.A: TCP usually has more protocol overhead, but neither is universally faster in every workload.
explanations.B: Both TCP and UDP use port numbers; the port namespaces are separate, but this is not the key distinction.
explanations.C: TCP establishes a connection and maintains transport state, while UDP sends independent datagrams.
explanations.D: Both TCP and UDP normally operate over IP.

questions.question: Which command can be used to display the current TCP/IP network configuration?

explanations.A: This Windows command displays detailed TCP/IP configuration including addresses, gateways, DNS servers, and adapter information.
explanations.B: Many operating systems use netstat -r to display routing information.
explanations.C: This displays cached ARP mappings rather than the MAC address directly configured on every local interface.
explanations.D: tracert on Windows discovers the path toward a destination by using packets with increasing TTL values.

questions.question: What does the netstat command do?

options.A: Displays network connections, routing tables, and statistics

explanations.A: netstat reports active connections, listening ports, routing tables, and network statistics depending on its options.
explanations.B: Interface configuration is handled by commands such as ipconfig, ifconfig, or ip.
explanations.C: ping is the common command for testing basic reachability.
explanations.D: Firewall configuration uses firewall-specific tools, not netstat.

questions.question: Which command is used to test connectivity to a specific IP address and trace the path the packets take?

explanations.A: ping tests reachability using ICMP Echo messages but does not trace every hop in the path.
explanations.B: arp displays or manipulates the ARP cache; it does not trace packet paths.
explanations.C: tracert on Windows discovers the path toward a destination by using packets with increasing TTL values.
explanations.D: nslookup queries DNS records and is used primarily for name-resolution troubleshooting.

questions.question: A device is unable to connect to any network. Which OSI layer should be investigated first?

explanations.A: The TCP/IP Application layer combines functions represented by several upper OSI layers.
explanations.B: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.C: The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing, but a complete inability to connect should first be checked at the Physical layer.
explanations.D: This is the answer highlighted in the supplied PYQ and directly addresses the question.

questions.question: If a computer can connect to local devices but not to the Internet, what might be misconfigured?

explanations.A: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.B: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.C: The default gateway is used to reach destinations outside the local subnet, so a wrong gateway can allow LAN access but block Internet access.
explanations.D: A MAC address identifies a network interface at Layer 2 and is not normally the setting that controls Internet routing.

questions.question: A web application can send data but cannot receive. What layer could be malfunctioning?

explanations.A: The TCP/IP Application layer combines functions represented by several upper OSI layers.
explanations.B: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.C: TCP can provide reliability through sequencing, acknowledgments, retransmission, and ordering.
explanations.D: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the MAC (Media Access Control) sublayer?

options.C: Controlling access to the physical medium

explanations.A: Frame delimiting identifies frame boundaries at the Data Link layer, but it is not the primary role of the MAC sublayer.
explanations.B: Ethernet frame error detection uses mechanisms such as the FCS; this is primarily associated with the frame/MAC processing.
explanations.C: The MAC sublayer coordinates access to the shared medium and defines media-access rules.
explanations.D: MAC addresses are physical/link-layer addresses, but the MAC sublayer's primary role is media access control.

questions.question: What is the standard Ethernet frame size for most networks?

explanations.A: Traditional Ethernet frames have a minimum size of 64 bytes and a maximum standard size of 1518 bytes excluding certain extensions.
explanations.B: These values are not the standard Ethernet frame-size range.
explanations.C: 1500 bytes is commonly the Ethernet payload MTU, not the full frame-size range.
explanations.D: This omits the standard Ethernet minimum frame size and describes neither the full frame range nor payload alone.

questions.question: In Ethernet networks, what is the purpose of the collision detection mechanism?

options.C: To detect and manage when two devices try to send data simultaneously

explanations.A: Plain HTTP does not encrypt traffic; HTTPS/TLS provides encryption.
explanations.B: Certificates do not compress network data.
explanations.C: Collision detection identifies simultaneous transmissions on shared Ethernet and triggers appropriate retransmission behavior.
explanations.D: Traffic prioritization is handled by QoS mechanisms, not collision detection.

questions.question: Which Ethernet standard provides a speed of 1 Gbps?

explanations.A: 10Base-T provides 10 Mbps Ethernet over twisted pair.
explanations.B: 100Base-TX provides 100 Mbps Ethernet.
explanations.C: 1000Base-T is Gigabit Ethernet and provides 1 Gbps over twisted pair.
explanations.D: 10GBase-T provides 10 Gbps Ethernet.

questions.question: What type of cable is used for most modern Ethernet networks?

explanations.A: Coaxial cable was widely used by early Ethernet variants but is not the usual medium for modern switched Ethernet LANs.
explanations.B: Fiber is common for high-speed and backbone Ethernet links, though copper is also widespread for endpoint connections.
explanations.C: Twisted-pair copper, such as Cat5e/Cat6, is widely used for modern Ethernet endpoint connections.
explanations.D: A valid modern Ethernet medium is included among the preceding choices.

questions.question: What does the term "full-duplex" mean in the context of Ethernet networking?

options.A: Data can be transmitted in one direction only
options.B: Data can be transmitted in both directions, but not simultaneously
options.C: Data can be transmitted in both directions simultaneously

explanations.A: One-way transmission describes simplex communication, not full-duplex.
explanations.B: This describes half-duplex communication.
explanations.C: Full-duplex permits simultaneous transmission and reception.
explanations.D: A valid modern Ethernet medium is included among the preceding choices.

questions.question: How does a switch determine the destination of an Ethernet frame?

options.A: By using the source IP address
options.B: By using the destination MAC address
options.C: By using the source MAC address
options.D: By broadcasting to all ports except the source

explanations.A: Ethernet switching decisions are based on Layer-2 MAC addresses rather than IP addresses.
explanations.B: A switch looks up the destination MAC address in its MAC/CAM table to select the outgoing port.
explanations.C: The source MAC is learned into the switch table, but it is not the primary destination-selection field.
explanations.D: Unknown-destination frames may be flooded, but a learned destination is normally forwarded only toward its known port.

questions.question: What mechanism do Ethernet switches use to avoid collisions?

explanations.A: Traditional shared half-duplex Ethernet used CSMA/CD; modern switched full-duplex Ethernet normally avoids collisions by eliminating the shared collision domain.
explanations.B: Switches provide separate collision domains per port and normally operate full-duplex, preventing normal Ethernet collisions.
explanations.C: Collision avoidance is associated more directly with wireless CSMA/CA than Ethernet switching.
explanations.D: This is a general phrase rather than the specific switching mechanism identified in the source.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes managed switches from unmanaged switches in an Ethernet network?

options.B: The ability to be configured and monitored

explanations.A: Managed status does not inherently mean a switch can encrypt all traffic.
explanations.B: Managed switches expose configuration, monitoring, VLAN, port, and management features that unmanaged switches generally lack.
explanations.C: Both managed and unmanaged switches may support copper or fiber depending on model.
explanations.D: Protocol support varies by model and is not the defining distinction between managed and unmanaged switches.

questions.question: Which command can be used to display the MAC address of a network interface on a Windows machine?

explanations.A: This Windows command displays detailed TCP/IP configuration including addresses, gateways, DNS servers, and adapter information.
explanations.B: ifconfig is a traditional Unix/Linux command for viewing and configuring network interfaces.
explanations.C: This displays cached ARP mappings rather than the MAC address directly configured on every local interface.
explanations.D: netstat -e displays Ethernet statistics on Windows; it is not the standard command for listing the local interface MAC address.

questions.question: On a Linux system, which command shows the MAC address of all network interfaces?

explanations.A: ip addr displays interface addresses and state, not the list of UDP sockets.
explanations.B: ifconfig lists interfaces and addresses but does not list listening TCP ports.
explanations.C: route primarily displays/manages routing information.
explanations.D: netstat -i displays interface statistics, but ifconfig -a is the source's selected command for showing MAC addresses.

questions.question: How can you change the MAC address of a network interface on Linux?

explanations.A: A persistent MAC-address change can be made through network configuration, depending on the Linux distribution and network manager.
explanations.B: ifconfig manages interfaces and addresses; it is not the standard modern command for adding routes.
explanations.C: macchanger is a dedicated Linux utility for changing/spoofing an interface MAC address.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: If a device is not receiving an IP address via DHCP over Ethernet, what layer should be investigated?

explanations.A: The TCP/IP Application layer combines functions represented by several upper OSI layers.
explanations.B: This option describes a different concept and therefore does not match the condition asked in the question.
explanations.C: The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing, but a complete inability to connect should first be checked at the Physical layer.
explanations.D: DHCP uses application-layer messages carried over UDP/IP, but successful Ethernet communication first depends on the Data Link layer being operational.

questions.question: A computer can access local network devices but not the internet. What should be checked on the switch?

explanations.A: Incorrect VLAN membership or trunk configuration can isolate a switch port from the routed/Internet VLAN while local devices in the same VLAN remain reachable.
explanations.B: Speed/duplex mismatches can reduce performance, but they are not the source's primary check for this symptom.
explanations.C: Power problems would generally cause loss of link rather than selective Internet-only failure.
explanations.D: Firmware can affect stability, but VLAN configuration is a more direct switch-level check for the stated symptom.

questions.question: What could be a reason for slow data transfer rates over an Ethernet network?

explanations.A: A faulty network interface can cause errors, packet loss, and reduced throughput.
explanations.B: Excessive cable length can cause attenuation/errors and reduce effective performance.
explanations.C: A duplex mismatch can cause collisions, retransmissions, and poor throughput.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Internet Protocol (IP)?

options.A: To provide error checking and correction

explanations.A: IP is best-effort and does not provide reliable error correction like TCP.
explanations.B: Reliable delivery is provided by protocols such as TCP, not by IP itself.
explanations.C: IP supplies logical addressing and enables packets to be routed between networks.
explanations.D: IP defines packet headers and addressing, but data formatting is not its primary purpose.

questions.question: What type of messages are used by ICMP to inform senders of network issues?

explanations.A: ICMP has query/informational messages, but the source is asking about messages that report network problems.
explanations.B: ICMP communicates errors and diagnostics such as destination unreachable and time exceeded.
explanations.C: Routing protocols such as OSPF or BGP exchange routing information; ICMP is not primarily a routing-update protocol.
explanations.D: This is not the standard ICMP message category for reporting network failures.

questions.question: Which IP protocol version uses 128-bit addresses?

explanations.A: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses.
explanations.B: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.
explanations.C: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses on local links.
explanations.D: RARP is unrelated to IPv6 security and is obsolete for normal IP address resolution.

questions.question: How do routers utilize ICMP messages within the IP framework?

explanations.A: AS_PATH is routing metadata, not an encryption mechanism.
explanations.B: ICMP does not normally prioritize traffic.
explanations.C: Routers and hosts use ICMP diagnostics such as Time Exceeded and Destination Unreachable to identify path problems.
explanations.D: ICMP does not provide packet compression.

questions.question: What is the main difference between IPv4 and IPv6?

explanations.A: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses while IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, making address size the fundamental difference listed.
explanations.B: Both versions have error-related mechanisms, but address size is the key difference asked here.
explanations.C: Neither IPv4 nor IPv6 inherently provides all end-to-end encryption; IPsec support differs in implementation/details.
explanations.D: Both can carry transport protocols such as TCP and UDP.

questions.question: Which feature of IPv6 eliminates the need for NAT (Network Address Translation)?

explanations.A: IPv6 supports stateless address autoconfiguration, but that is not the feature that creates its large address capacity.
explanations.B: IPv6 was designed with IPsec support, but encryption is not what eliminates NAT.
explanations.C: IPv6's 128-bit address space provides enough globally routable addresses to reduce the address-exhaustion pressure that motivated widespread NAT.
explanations.D: IPv6 multicast is important for efficient group communication but does not itself eliminate the need for address translation.

questions.question: What is the function of an IP subnet mask?

options.A: To separate the network address from the host address

explanations.A: A subnet mask identifies which bits of an IP address represent the network/subnet portion and which represent the host portion.
explanations.B: Subnet masks perform addressing calculations and do not encrypt data.
explanations.C: IP conflict detection is handled by network protocols/tools, not by the subnet mask itself.
explanations.D: DHCP can assign IP addresses; a subnet mask only defines the network/host boundary.

questions.question: In IPv6, what is the equivalent of ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) used in IPv4?

explanations.A: DHCPv6 provides IPv6 configuration services but does not replace ARP's neighbor-resolution function.
explanations.B: ICMPv6 provides control, diagnostics, and Neighbor Discovery; it is not the IPsec integrity/authentication mechanism.
explanations.C: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery replaces ARP-style address resolution using ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement messages.
explanations.D: IGMP is an IPv4 multicast-management protocol; IPv6 uses ICMPv6 mechanisms for multicast listener management.

questions.question: What mechanism does IPv6 use to ensure data integrity and authentication?

explanations.A: ESP can provide confidentiality plus integrity/authentication in IPsec, but the source marks AH for the stated integrity/authentication mechanism.
explanations.B: IPsec AH provides integrity and authentication of IP packets but does not provide encryption.
explanations.C: ICMPv6 provides control, diagnostics, and Neighbor Discovery; it is not the IPsec integrity/authentication mechanism.
explanations.D: RARP is unrelated to IPv6 security and is obsolete for normal IP address resolution.

questions.question: How can you display the current IP configuration on a Unix/Linux system?

explanations.A: ipconfig is a Windows command used to display and manage IP configuration.
explanations.B: ifconfig is a traditional Unix/Linux command for viewing and configuring network interfaces.
explanations.C: netstat -i displays interface statistics, but ifconfig -a is the source's selected command for showing MAC addresses.
explanations.D: This displays cached ARP mappings rather than the MAC address directly configured on every local interface.

questions.question: Which command can you use to test IPv6 connectivity to an address?

explanations.A: ping6 sends ICMPv6 Echo Requests to test IPv6 reachability on systems that provide the command.
explanations.B: tracert6 is a Windows-style IPv6 trace command on some systems, but it is not the source's selected basic connectivity test.
explanations.C: This syntax is not the standard cross-platform command for testing IPv6 connectivity.
explanations.D: ifconfig configures/displays interfaces; it does not itself test end-to-end IPv6 connectivity.

questions.question: What command provides detailed information about routes to an IPv6 address and discovers MTU along the path?

explanations.A: mtr combines ping and traceroute-style measurements, but the source selects tracepath6 for IPv6 path and MTU discovery.
explanations.B: tracepath6 traces an IPv6 path and can discover the path MTU using packet-size probing.
explanations.C: This displays IPv6 routing information but does not perform the path MTU discovery described.
explanations.D: This can display IPv6 routing information on some systems but is not the source's path/MTU-discovery command.

questions.question: A computer can access IPv4 websites but not IPv6 websites. What should be checked first?

explanations.A: If IPv6 websites fail while IPv4 works, local IPv6 addressing, routes, and interface configuration should be checked first.
explanations.B: Router IPv6 support matters, but local configuration is the first direct check on the affected computer.
explanations.C: DNS problems can affect name resolution, but IPv6 connectivity itself can be tested with a literal IPv6 address.
explanations.D: A firewall can block IPv6 traffic, but the source prioritizes checking the host's IPv6 configuration.

questions.question: You're unable to ping an IPv6 address from your machine. What could be the issue?

explanations.A: A bad subnet mask can cause reachability problems but is not the source's likely cause of delayed connection establishment.
explanations.B: Blocking ICMPv6 can prevent ping and can also disrupt important IPv6 control functions.
explanations.C: A wrong IPv6 default gateway can prevent communication with remote networks.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: How to resolve intermittent connectivity issues with an IPv6 network?

options.C: Checking for IPv6 prefix delegation issues

explanations.A: Replacing hardware may solve a hardware fault but is not the first universal troubleshooting step.
explanations.B: Updated drivers/firmware can fix interoperability and stability problems, but the source emphasizes prefix delegation.
explanations.C: Incorrect or unstable prefix delegation can cause hosts to receive invalid/changed IPv6 prefixes and intermittent connectivity.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of routing protocols in a network?

explanations.A: Plain HTTP does not encrypt traffic; HTTPS/TLS provides encryption.
explanations.B: Certificates do not compress network data.
explanations.C: Routing protocols exchange information and calculate/select paths through a network.
explanations.D: User authorization is handled by identity and access-control systems, not routing protocols.

questions.question: Which type of routing algorithm does OSPF use?

explanations.A: Distance-vector protocols use information about destination distance and next hop from neighbors.
explanations.B: OSPF is a link-state protocol: routers build a topology database and calculate shortest paths.
explanations.C: BGP is a path-vector protocol, not OSPF.
explanations.D: Some protocols combine characteristics, but OSPF is classified as link-state.

questions.question: What differentiates dynamic routing from static routing?

explanations.A: Security depends on configuration and protocol protections; dynamic routing is not inherently less secure.
explanations.B: Static routes are manually configured and do not automatically adapt to topology changes.
explanations.C: Dynamic protocols learn and recalculate routes as network conditions/topology change.
explanations.D: Static routing can have low processing overhead, but speed is not the defining difference asked here.

questions.question: In BGP (Border Gateway Protocol), what is the main factor in selecting the best path?

explanations.A: BGP considers path attributes and policy; path length alone is not the complete best-path criterion.
explanations.B: Bandwidth can influence some IGP metrics but is not the primary universal BGP selection factor.
explanations.C: BGP is policy-driven and does not simply choose the numerically lowest cost.
explanations.D: The AS_PATH attribute records traversed autonomous systems and path length is an important BGP selection factor; the source marks AS-hop count.

questions.question: How does a distance-vector routing protocol determine the best route?

explanations.A: Classic RIP-style distance-vector routing uses hop count as its metric.
explanations.B: Latency is not the basic metric used by RIP's classic distance-vector calculation.
explanations.C: Bandwidth can influence certain routing metrics, but classic distance-vector RIP uses hop count.
explanations.D: Some distance-vector protocols use a metric, but the source specifically identifies hop counting.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using a routing protocol like EIGRP compared to RIP?

explanations.A: EIGRP generally converges faster than RIP because of its more sophisticated route computation and update mechanisms.
explanations.B: Traditional FTP is not inherently more secure than HTTP; both require additional security mechanisms for protected transfer.
explanations.C: RIP is generally simpler, so this does not describe EIGRP's primary advantage.
explanations.D: EIGRP can be efficient with updates, but the source's principal distinction is faster convergence.

questions.question: Which routing protocol is classified as an Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP)?

explanations.A: OSPF is an Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) used within an autonomous system.
explanations.B: EIGRP is an IGP used within an autonomous system.
explanations.C: BGP is the standard inter-domain routing protocol and is classified as an EGP.
explanations.D: RIP is an IGP using distance-vector routing.

questions.question: What mechanism does OSPF use to prevent routing loops?

explanations.A: Split horizon is a loop-prevention technique used by distance-vector protocols.
explanations.B: Route poisoning advertises an unreachable route with an infinite metric and helps prevent loops in distance-vector routing.
explanations.C: OSPF floods LSAs to build a consistent link-state database used for shortest-path computation.
explanations.D: OSPF areas organize the topology and reduce routing-information scope; the source marks area designations as the loop-prevention mechanism.

questions.question: In BGP, what is the purpose of the AS_PATH attribute?

options.B: To specify the priority of routes
options.C: To record the path of ASes

explanations.A: AS_PATH is routing metadata, not an encryption mechanism.
explanations.B: BGP route preference can involve multiple attributes, while AS_PATH specifically records AS traversal.
explanations.C: AS_PATH lists the autonomous systems a BGP route advertisement has traversed.
explanations.D: The route source can be represented by other BGP information; AS_PATH records AS traversal.

questions.question: Which command can display the routing table on a Cisco router?

explanations.A: Cisco IOS uses show ip route to display the IPv4 routing table.
explanations.B: This is a common command on some other network operating systems, not the Cisco IOS command identified in the source.
explanations.C: Windows uses route print to display its routing table.
explanations.D: Many operating systems use netstat -r to display routing information.

questions.question: How can you manually add a static route to the routing table in Linux?

options.D: Using the ip route add command

explanations.A: The legacy route utility can add static routes on Linux systems that provide it.
explanations.B: ifconfig manages interfaces and addresses; it is not the standard modern command for adding routes.
explanations.C: The hosts file maps names to addresses and does not add kernel routing entries.
explanations.D: The modern Linux ip utility uses 'ip route add' to create a static route.

questions.question: In Cisco IOS, how can you redistribute OSPF routes into EIGRP?

options.A: By configuring redistribution in the OSPF process
options.B: By configuring redistribution in the EIGRP process

explanations.A: To send OSPF-learned routes into EIGRP, redistribution is configured under the destination EIGRP routing process.
explanations.B: The EIGRP process is where routes from OSPF can be redistributed into EIGRP.
explanations.C: Access lists can filter traffic/routes but do not by themselves perform routing-protocol redistribution.
explanations.D: Route maps can control and modify redistribution policy, but the redistribution command belongs under the target routing process.

questions.question: If a newly added network is not appearing in the routing tables, what should be checked first?

explanations.A: A new network can be absent because of a physical problem, but the source first points to route advertisements.
explanations.B: Summarization can hide specific routes, but it is not always the first check for a newly added network.
explanations.C: ACLs can affect redistribution or traffic, but they are not the fundamental mechanism for advertising a newly added network.
explanations.D: Routing protocols must advertise/learn the new network before other routers can install it in their routing tables.

questions.question: A router is not choosing the expected path for traffic, what might be misconfigured?

explanations.A: Bandwidth settings can influence metrics and path selection in some routing protocols.
explanations.B: Administrative distance and protocol-specific preferences can affect which learned route is selected.
explanations.C: An incorrect next hop can make a route unusable or lead traffic along an unexpected path.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: How can you resolve a persistent routing loop between two routers?

explanations.A: Raising a hop-count limit can delay loop detection rather than fix the underlying loop.
explanations.B: Hold-down timers help suppress unstable updates in distance-vector protocols, but the source selects route filtering for a persistent two-router loop.
explanations.C: Mask mismatches can create routing problems but are not the source's general loop-prevention answer.
explanations.D: Route filtering can prevent problematic route advertisements from creating persistent loops.

questions.question: What is the main difference between TCP and UDP?

options.A: TCP is connectionless, while UDP is connection-oriented
options.B: TCP is connection-oriented, while UDP is connectionless
options.D: UDP is more secure than TCP

explanations.A: This reverses the properties of TCP and UDP.
explanations.B: TCP establishes a connection and maintains state; UDP sends connectionless datagrams.
explanations.C: TCP usually has more protocol overhead, but neither is universally faster in every workload.
explanations.D: Neither protocol is inherently secure; encryption is provided by higher-layer/security mechanisms.

questions.question: Which protocol is typically used for streaming media?

explanations.A: TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered byte-stream delivery.
explanations.B: UDP is connectionless and does not provide TCP-style reliability or ordering.
explanations.C: SCTP is a transport protocol with message-oriented features, but it is not the source's typical streaming-media choice.
explanations.D: RTP is commonly used to carry real-time audio/video, usually over UDP, but the source marks UDP as the transport protocol.

questions.question: How does TCP ensure data is delivered reliably and in the correct order?

options.B: By using sequence numbers and acknowledgments

explanations.A: Checksums detect corruption, while TCP reliability additionally relies on sequencing, acknowledgments, and retransmission.
explanations.B: Sequence numbers enable ordering and acknowledgments confirm received data, allowing retransmission of missing segments.
explanations.C: Compression reduces size and does not provide reliable delivery or ordering.
explanations.D: Encryption protects confidentiality and does not itself provide TCP reliability or ordering.

questions.question: In TCP, what mechanism is used to control the rate of data transmission to prevent network congestion?

explanations.A: TCP detects loss/errors and retransmits data rather than using application-independent forward error correction as its main reliability mechanism.
explanations.B: TCP flow control uses the receiver's advertised window to prevent a sender from overwhelming the receiver; congestion control separately addresses network congestion.
explanations.C: Encryption is unrelated to TCP rate control.
explanations.D: HTTP/2 supports header compression with HPACK, but multiplexing is the mechanism that reduces head-of-line request serialization and improves parallel loading.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a TCP three-way handshake?

options.B: To synchronize sequence numbers and acknowledge the connection

explanations.A: The TCP three-way handshake establishes a transport connection but does not itself provide encryption/security.
explanations.B: SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK exchange establishes state and synchronizes initial sequence numbers.
explanations.C: Certificates do not compress network data.
explanations.D: Plain HTTP does not encrypt traffic; HTTPS/TLS provides encryption.

questions.question: Which TCP header field is used for flow control?

explanations.A: Sequence numbers identify the position of TCP data and support ordering/retransmission, not direct receiver-rate control.
explanations.B: The acknowledgment number indicates the next byte expected and confirms received data.
explanations.C: The advertised TCP window indicates how much data the receiver can accept without further acknowledgment, providing flow control.
explanations.D: The TCP checksum detects corruption in the TCP segment.

questions.question: How does UDP handle error checking?

options.A: It uses sequence numbers and acknowledgments
options.B: It includes a checksum for error detection

explanations.A: UDP has no TCP-style sequence/acknowledgment mechanism.
explanations.B: UDP includes a checksum field for detecting corruption; it does not guarantee delivery or retransmission.
explanations.C: UDP provides no built-in encryption.
explanations.D: UDP provides no built-in compression.

questions.question: What is TCP's initial congestion window size typically set to?

explanations.A: The source does not use this value for the typical initial congestion window in this question.
explanations.B: Two MSS is not the source's selected typical value.
explanations.C: The source marks three MSS as the typical initial congestion-window size; actual TCP implementations can vary by RFC/version.
explanations.D: Four MSS is not the source's selected value.

questions.question: In TCP, what is the function of the congestion avoidance algorithm?

options.A: To reduce the data transmission rate before packet loss occurs
options.D: To ensure data is sent in order

explanations.A: Congestion avoidance increases the sending rate cautiously and responds to signs of congestion to limit overload.
explanations.B: Plain HTTP does not encrypt traffic; HTTPS/TLS provides encryption.
explanations.C: Certificates do not compress network data.
explanations.D: Ordering is handled by TCP sequence numbers and reassembly, not the congestion-avoidance algorithm.

questions.question: How can you check open TCP ports on a Windows machine?

explanations.A: On Windows, netstat -an lists active connections and listening ports without resolving names, making it useful for checking open TCP ports.
explanations.B: This Windows command displays detailed TCP/IP configuration including addresses, gateways, DNS servers, and adapter information.
explanations.C: ifconfig lists interfaces and addresses but does not list listening TCP ports.
explanations.D: traceroute discovers network paths rather than listing local listening TCP ports.

questions.question: In Linux, how can you view the UDP sockets currently in use?

explanations.A: netstat -au on Linux displays UDP sockets and listening UDP endpoints.
explanations.B: ifconfig is a traditional Unix/Linux command for viewing and configuring network interfaces.
explanations.C: ip addr displays interface addresses and state, not the list of UDP sockets.
explanations.D: ss -u also displays UDP sockets on Linux, but the source marks netstat -au.

questions.question: How can you set a specific TCP window size when using the iperf command for testing?

explanations.A: The -w option sets the TCP window/socket-buffer size used by iperf testing.
explanations.B: This starts iperf in server/listening mode and does not specify the TCP window size.
explanations.C: This starts an iperf client connection to the specified host; it does not itself set the window size.
explanations.D: The -l option controls buffer length, not the TCP window setting represented by -w.

questions.question: If a client is experiencing delayed TCP connections, what could be a potential cause?

explanations.A: A bad subnet mask can cause reachability problems but is not the source's likely cause of delayed connection establishment.
explanations.B: If a client connects using hostnames, slow DNS resolution can make the apparent TCP connection setup feel delayed.
explanations.C: Incorrect routes can cause packets to take inefficient paths or fail to reach the destination.
explanations.D: A firewall can block FTP connections, but a server-side permission error more directly points to credentials/permissions.

questions.question: A UDP-based application is experiencing packet loss. What should be investigated first?

explanations.A: Application-level handling can affect how loss is reported/recovered, but UDP packet loss should first prompt network-path investigation.
explanations.B: Congestion can slow or interrupt transfer but does not directly explain an FTP permission-denied response.
explanations.C: A wrong port usually causes delivery failure rather than random packet loss.
explanations.D: A firewall can block FTP connections, but a server-side permission error more directly points to credentials/permissions.

questions.question: How can you troubleshoot intermittent TCP connection timeouts?

explanations.A: Bad NICs, cables, switches, or interfaces can cause intermittent TCP failures.
explanations.B: Longer timeouts may mask symptoms but do not necessarily fix the network cause.
explanations.C: Packet loss, route flaps, and unstable links can cause intermittent TCP timeouts.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: What is the primary function of HTTP in the web architecture?

explanations.A: Plain HTTP does not encrypt traffic; HTTPS/TLS provides encryption.
explanations.B: Certificates do not compress network data.
explanations.C: HTTP defines request/response communication for web resources, historically including hypertext documents.
explanations.D: HTTP can deliver video, but streaming is an application use rather than HTTP's primary purpose.

questions.question: FTP uses which mode for establishing data connections by default?

explanations.A: Traditional FTP uses active mode by default in the source: the server opens the data connection back toward the client.
explanations.B: Passive FTP has the client initiate both control and data connections and is often easier through firewalls/NAT, but it is not the source's default.
explanations.C: Secure FTP is not an FTP connection mode; FTPS/SFTP are distinct secure mechanisms.
explanations.D: Anonymous login is an authentication mode, not a data-connection establishment mode.

questions.question: Which of the following HTTP methods is idempotent and used for updating resources on a server?

explanations.A: GET is safe and idempotent and normally retrieves a representation rather than updating a resource.
explanations.B: POST is generally not idempotent and is commonly used to create resources or trigger processing.
explanations.C: PUT is idempotent and is commonly used to create or replace a resource at a specified URI.
explanations.D: DELETE is also defined as idempotent, but the source specifically associates updating/replacing resources with PUT.

questions.question: In HTTP, what status code indicates that the requested resource has been permanently moved to a new URL?

explanations.A: 200 indicates successful processing of the request.
explanations.B: 301 indicates that the resource has been permanently assigned a new URI and clients may use the new location.
explanations.C: 404 means the server could not find the requested resource.
explanations.D: 500 indicates an unexpected server-side error.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using FTP over HTTP for file transfer?

options.C: Support for directory listing and manipulation

explanations.A: Traditional FTP is not inherently more secure than HTTP; both require additional security mechanisms for protected transfer.
explanations.B: FTP is not inherently a better compression protocol than HTTP.
explanations.C: FTP provides commands specifically designed for remote file and directory management.
explanations.D: Transfer speed depends on implementation and network conditions rather than being an inherent FTP advantage.

questions.question: What mechanism does HTTP/2 use to reduce latency and improve load times compared to HTTP/1.1?

explanations.A: HTTP/2 supports header compression with HPACK, but multiplexing is the mechanism that reduces head-of-line request serialization and improves parallel loading.
explanations.B: HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple streams over one connection, reducing the need for multiple parallel TCP connections.
explanations.C: HTTP/2 can be used with TLS, but encryption is not the mechanism that differentiates its stream multiplexing performance.
explanations.D: Tokenization is not the HTTP/2 latency mechanism.

questions.question: How does FTP ensure data is transferred securely?

explanations.A: FTP itself is not secure; FTP over TLS (FTPS) can encrypt the control/data channels.
explanations.B: Compression can reduce transfer size but does not by itself secure FTP.
explanations.C: Checksums can detect accidental corruption but do not provide confidentiality/authentication comparable to TLS.
explanations.D: FTP uses TCP, not UDP, and UDP does not inherently provide security.

questions.question: Which feature of HTTP/3 aims to improve performance over lossy or unreliable networks?

explanations.A: HTTP/3 runs over QUIC, which provides stream multiplexing and loss recovery over UDP and performs well on changing/lossy paths.
explanations.B: WebSocket is a separate bidirectional communication protocol and is not the core HTTP/3 transport feature.
explanations.C: Server Push was an HTTP feature associated with HTTP/2 and is not the primary HTTP/3 improvement for lossy networks.
explanations.D: Content-Encoding describes payload transformations such as gzip or Brotli, not the transport-level improvement supplied by QUIC.

questions.question: In FTP, what is the difference between binary and ASCII transfer modes?

options.A: Binary mode transfers files as text, while ASCII mode transfers them as binary
options.B: Binary mode compresses data, while ASCII mode does not
options.C: Binary mode transfers files in a binary format without conversion, while ASCII mode converts files between different text formats
options.D: Binary mode is more secure than ASCII mode

explanations.A: This reverses the definitions of FTP binary and ASCII modes.
explanations.B: Binary/ASCII mode changes representation/translation behavior, not compression.
explanations.C: Binary preserves byte values; ASCII mode may translate text line endings/representations between systems.
explanations.D: Neither transfer mode inherently provides security; encryption is a separate concern.

questions.question: How can you download a file from an FTP server using the command line in Linux?

explanations.A: wget can retrieve files from FTP URLs from the Linux command line when FTP support is available.
explanations.B: curl -O can download an FTP resource while preserving the remote filename.
explanations.C: The ftp client can connect interactively and retrieve files, but the source marks wget for the direct download command.
explanations.D: scp uses SSH/SFTP-style secure copy and does not use an FTP URL as an FTP client.

questions.question: How can you send a custom HTTP header with a curl request?

explanations.A: curl -d sends request body data and is not the standard option for adding a custom HTTP header.
explanations.B: curl -H/--header adds a custom HTTP header and value to the request.
explanations.C: curl --header is also a valid long-form option for adding a header; the source's marked form includes the explicit header value.
explanations.D: curl does not use --custom-header as its standard option for arbitrary HTTP headers.

questions.question: What command allows you to interactively communicate with an HTTP server using telnet?

explanations.A: Telnet to TCP port 80 can be used to manually send a plain HTTP request such as GET / HTTP/1.1.
explanations.B: Port 443 normally expects TLS, so a plain telnet HTTP exchange will not provide a normal HTTPS session.
explanations.C: POST is valid HTTP, but GET is the simplest standard request for interactively retrieving a page in this example.
explanations.D: HEAD is a valid HTTP method, but the source uses GET for the interactive demonstration.

questions.question: If a web page is not loading correctly, what should be checked first?

explanations.A: A stale or corrupted browser cache can cause a page to render incorrectly even when network access is working.
explanations.B: Server misconfiguration can cause page failures, but basic local/network connectivity is a reasonable first diagnostic check.
explanations.C: Incorrect DNS can prevent hostnames from resolving, but the source marks the basic network connection as the first check.
explanations.D: If a page cannot load, verifying that the device has working network connectivity establishes whether the problem is local to the connection.

questions.question: A file transfer via FTP fails with a permission error. What is likely the cause?

options.C: File not found on the server

explanations.A: FTP permission/authentication errors commonly occur when the supplied credentials are invalid or lack required permissions.
explanations.B: Congestion can slow or interrupt transfer but does not directly explain an FTP permission-denied response.
explanations.C: A missing file normally produces a file-not-found error rather than a permission error.
explanations.D: A firewall can block FTP connections, but a server-side permission error more directly points to credentials/permissions.

questions.question: How can you diagnose slow FTP file transfers?

explanations.A: Large files and inefficient formats can influence transfer time and should be considered during diagnosis.
explanations.B: Available bandwidth and congestion directly affect FTP throughput.
explanations.C: High server CPU, disk, or connection load can reduce transfer performance.
explanations.D: The source treats hardware, timeout configuration, and path stability as possible troubleshooting areas.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a firewall in network security?

options.B: To manage network traffic based on rules

explanations.A: Antivirus software performs malware detection/removal; a firewall primarily filters network traffic.
explanations.B: A firewall permits or blocks traffic based on addresses, ports, protocols, state, and configured policies.
explanations.C: Encryption is normally provided by TLS, IPsec, VPNs, or application-level cryptography rather than a basic firewall.
explanations.D: Authentication can be integrated with some security systems, but it is not the primary purpose of a firewall.

questions.question: Which cryptographic algorithm is commonly used for secure password storage?

explanations.A: RSA is an asymmetric public-key algorithm used for signatures/key operations; it is not a password-hashing function.
explanations.B: AES is a symmetric encryption algorithm, not a password-hashing algorithm.
explanations.C: SHA-256 is a cryptographic hash function and has historically been used for password hashing, although modern password storage should use a dedicated password KDF such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt.
explanations.D: DES is an obsolete symmetric block cipher and is not suitable for modern password storage.

questions.question: What is the function of a digital certificate in network security?

options.B: To verify the identity of entities exchanging information online

explanations.A: Certificates can bind identity to a public key and are used in authentication; integrity is provided by signatures/TLS mechanisms associated with the certificate.
explanations.B: Digital certificates bind an entity's identity to a public key and are validated through a certificate authority trust chain.
explanations.C: Certificates do not compress network data.
explanations.D: Certificates do not increase raw transfer speed.

questions.question: What differentiates symmetric from asymmetric encryption?

options.A: The use of one key for encryption and a different key for decryption
options.B: The speed of encryption and decryption
options.D: The use of a single key for both encryption and decryption

explanations.A: This describes asymmetric/public-key cryptography rather than symmetric encryption.
explanations.B: Symmetric algorithms are generally faster, but speed is not the defining cryptographic distinction in the question.
explanations.C: Algorithm family differs, but the fundamental distinction is how keys are used.
explanations.D: Symmetric cryptography uses the same shared secret key for both encryption and decryption.

questions.question: In the context of cryptography, what is a nonce?

explanations.A: A nonce is a value intended to be used once in a particular cryptographic context to prevent replay/reuse problems.
explanations.B: A nonce is an input/value, not an encryption algorithm itself.
explanations.C: A nonce is not a digital-signature type.
explanations.D: A nonce is not a communication protocol.

questions.question: How does a public key infrastructure (PKI) enhance network security?

options.A: By providing digital certificates that verify the ownership of public keys
options.B: By encrypting all data on the network

explanations.A: PKI uses certificates issued by trusted authorities to bind identities to public keys.
explanations.B: PKI supports authentication and key management; it does not automatically encrypt every network packet.
explanations.C: Intrusion detection systems perform that function.
explanations.D: Firewalls, routers, and QoS systems manage traffic; PKI's core role is trust/key management.

questions.question: What is the primary security concern addressed by HTTPS?

explanations.A: HTTPS can detect tampering and protect integrity, but the source focuses on interception/confidentiality during transmission.
explanations.B: HTTPS can help prevent impersonation through server authentication, but its primary transport security concern here is interception.
explanations.C: HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt traffic and authenticate the server, reducing the risk of eavesdropping/interception.
explanations.D: Access control mechanisms handle resource authorization; HTTPS secures a web connection.

questions.question: What role does the Diffie-Hellman algorithm play in cryptography?

options.A: It provides a method for digital signatures
options.B: It is used for secure password storage
options.C: It enables the secure exchange of encryption keys over a public channel

explanations.A: Diffie-Hellman is a key-agreement mechanism, not a digital-signature algorithm.
explanations.B: Password storage requires password-hashing/KDF techniques; Diffie-Hellman is not one.
explanations.C: Diffie-Hellman allows parties to derive a shared secret over an untrusted/public channel, subject to authentication against MitM attacks.
explanations.D: Diffie-Hellman establishes shared key material; it does not directly encrypt application data.

questions.question: How can you generate a 2048-bit RSA key pair using OpenSSL?

explanations.A: The modern genpkey syntax is valid in OpenSSL, but the key-size parameter normally needs an RSA parameter option; the source marks genrsa.
explanations.B: openssl rsa is primarily for processing existing RSA keys; this is not the standard key-generation syntax.
explanations.C: genrsa generates an RSA private key with the requested 2048-bit size in the source's command.
explanations.D: rsakey is not the standard OpenSSL command for RSA key generation.

questions.question: What command can be used to encrypt a file using AES-256-CBC with OpenSSL?

explanations.A: OpenSSL's AES encryption is normally invoked through the enc command; this form omits enc.
explanations.B: encrypt is not the standard OpenSSL command used for symmetric file encryption.
explanations.C: openssl enc invokes the symmetric cipher command and -aes-256-cbc selects AES-256-CBC with the supplied password.
explanations.D: The cipher is normally selected through openssl enc rather than as a top-level aes-256-cbc command.

questions.question: If an encrypted email cannot be decrypted by the recipient, what should be checked first?

options.A: The email client's compatibility with the encryption standard
options.B: The correctness of the recipient's public key
options.C: The strength of the encryption algorithm

explanations.A: Client compatibility can matter, but the source first checks the recipient key because encrypted email depends on the correct recipient key.
explanations.B: If the message was encrypted to an incorrect or mismatched recipient key, the intended private key cannot decrypt it.
explanations.C: Algorithm strength affects security, not whether a correctly addressed ciphertext can be decrypted.
explanations.D: A signature can fail independently of message decryption and is not the first check for an undecryptable message.

questions.question: How can network administrators detect and mitigate a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack?

explanations.A: Stronger encryption can protect confidentiality, but MitM prevention also requires authentication of endpoints.
explanations.B: Firewall rules can reduce some attacks but do not establish cryptographic endpoint authentication.
explanations.C: TLS certificates authenticate the server and HTTPS protects the connection against interception and tampering.
explanations.D: Monitoring can help detect anomalies and attacks but does not by itself prevent a MitM attack.

questions.question: Which frequency band is not commonly used by Wi-Fi networks?

explanations.A: 2.4 GHz is a common Wi-Fi band used by many IEEE 802.11 standards.
explanations.B: 5 GHz is a common Wi-Fi band with more channels and generally less interference than 2.4 GHz.
explanations.C: 900 MHz is not one of the standard mainstream Wi-Fi bands represented by common consumer 802.11 deployments.
explanations.D: 60 GHz is used by some Wi-Fi standards such as 802.11ad/ay, although it is much less common than 2.4/5 GHz.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Mobile IP protocol?

options.B: To manage mobile device power consumption
options.C: To enable devices to move across networks without losing connectivity
options.D: To compress data for faster transmission

explanations.A: Mobile IP is about maintaining reachability during mobility, not directly providing wireless encryption.
explanations.B: Power management is handled by mobile OS/radio technologies rather than Mobile IP.
explanations.C: Mobile IP maintains a stable home address/reachability while a device moves between networks.
explanations.D: Mobile IP does not compress application data.

questions.question: In the context of mobile computing, what is edge computing?

options.A: Processing data in a central data center
options.B: Storing data exclusively on the mobile device
options.C: Processing data near the source of data generation
options.D: Using cloud storage as the only data storage option

explanations.A: Centralized cloud/data-center processing is the opposite of the key edge-computing idea.
explanations.B: Local storage is not the defining feature of edge computing.
explanations.C: Edge computing moves computation closer to sensors/devices/users to reduce latency and backhaul traffic.
explanations.D: Edge architectures can still use cloud storage, but do not require it exclusively.

questions.question: Which technology underpins the LTE (Long Term Evolution) standard for mobile communication?

explanations.A: GSM is a cellular technology family and is not the multiple-access technology underlying LTE's radio interface.
explanations.B: CDMA is used by earlier cellular systems; LTE's downlink uses OFDMA.
explanations.C: LTE uses Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access on the downlink, enabling multiple users to share subcarriers.
explanations.D: TDMA is used in some older mobile systems but is not the LTE downlink multiple-access technique.

questions.question: How do MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) technologies improve wireless network performance?

options.B: By increasing the range of frequencies used
options.C: By using multiple antennas for transmission and reception

explanations.A: MIMO is a radio technique for spatial processing, not encryption.
explanations.B: MIMO uses spatial dimensions/multiple antennas rather than simply increasing the frequency range.
explanations.C: MIMO uses multiple transmit and receive antennas to exploit spatial diversity and/or multiplexing for better throughput/reliability.
explanations.D: MIMO does not compress application data.

questions.question: What challenge does the hidden node problem pose in wireless networks?

options.C: Interference and collision of data transmissions

explanations.A: The hidden-node problem is primarily about nodes being unable to sense one another, not general clock synchronization.
explanations.B: Hidden nodes create medium-access collisions; interception is a separate security issue.
explanations.C: Two hidden transmitters may transmit simultaneously because they cannot hear each other, causing interference/collisions at a receiver.
explanations.D: Energy use can be affected by retransmissions, but the defining problem is collision/interference.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using SDN (Software Defined Networking) in wireless networks?

explanations.A: SDN can enable centralized security policy, but enhanced security is not the primary advantage asked here.
explanations.B: SDN separates control logic from forwarding hardware, but the key benefit in the source is flexible management/configuration.
explanations.C: SDN centralizes/programmatically controls network behavior, making configuration and policy changes more flexible.
explanations.D: SDN can optimize traffic in some deployments but does not inherently increase physical link speed.
